assessment.nobel_worthiness: A powerful framework and empirical agenda linking firm-level distortions to aggregate productivity and cross-country income differences.
assessment.attribution: The listed trio provides a coherent, complementary body of conceptual, quantitative and measurement contributions.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has been extensively applied across countries and has become central to research on development and productivity.
uncertainties: Estimated distortion wedges may reflect forces other than allocative inefficiency, complicating welfare interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and made its distributional and aggregate implications empirically tractable.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplied the seminal heterogeneous-firm framework, with Helpman and Redding making major linked theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply embedded in trade research, quantitative policy analysis and empirical work.
uncertainties: The broader intellectual lineage contains further important contributors not represented in the three-name credit set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established management practices and organisational capital as measurable, economically consequential determinants of firm performance and productivity.
assessment.attribution: The proposed laureates form a closely connected body of work spanning measurement, causal evidence and applications.
assessment.maturity: The findings have accumulated across countries, sectors and policy settings over a substantial period.
uncertainties: Measurement and treatment effects can depend on context, and the boundaries between management, complementary inputs and selection remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work fundamentally reshaped understanding of how technology and trade shocks affect local labour markets, tasks and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson have a particularly identifiable joint contribution on labour-market adjustment to trade exposure, alongside related work on tasks.
assessment.maturity: Its empirical designs and conclusions have generated a large literature and remain highly consequential for policy analysis.
uncertainties: The relative weight of trade, technology and other local adjustment mechanisms varies across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models materially improved analysis of monetary and fiscal transmission by incorporating realistic household balance sheets and marginal propensities to consume.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll and Violante are central architects of the modern quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework is now widely used in macroeconomic research and policy-oriented quantitative work.
uncertainties: The core contributions are comparatively recent, and conclusions remain sensitive to household and financial-market modeling choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data research made intergenerational mobility measurable at fine geographic and institutional levels and changed the evidence base for opportunity policy.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are especially central to the measurement programme and its interpretation of place-based mobility differences.
assessment.maturity: The methods and findings have been replicated, extended and incorporated into a broad mobility literature.
uncertainties: Descriptive mobility differences do not by themselves identify the mechanisms or causal effects of places and policies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme on reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion changed economic models of behaviour and generated influential experimental evidence.
assessment.attribution: Fehr, Falk and Schmidt made closely connected theoretical and experimental contributions to the modern social-preferences literature.
assessment.maturity: The concepts have been tested across laboratory, field and organisational settings for decades.
uncertainties: The scope and stability of measured social preferences across contexts remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification supplied a disciplined alternative to unjustified point identification and broadened credible empirical inference under weak assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is foundational, while Tamer and Molinari made major contributions to moment inequalities and practical inference.
assessment.maturity: The approach is established across econometrics and applied microeconomics.
uncertainties: Its importance is methodological and diffuse, which may make a sharply bounded prize attribution more difficult.
